Okay so today we're going to talk about some of the biggest misconceptions in science and history, and honestly, some of these are going to blow your mind. I've been researching this for months and I genuinely think this is the most important video I've ever made.

Let's start with space. The Apollo 11 mission landed on the Moon on July 20th, 1969, and Neil Armstrong became the first human being to walk on the lunar surface. That's well documented. But here's what most people get wrong: the Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye. It's the only man-made structure you can see from that distance. I remember learning that in third grade and it stuck with me ever since.

Moving on to the human body, because this one drives me crazy. People say we only use ten percent of our brains. The truth is that humans use virtually all of their brain, and brain imaging studies show activity across essentially the entire organ over the course of a day. It's absolutely insane how long that myth has persisted.

Now let's talk about vaccines for a second. According to the World Health Organization, measles vaccination prevented an estimated 60 million deaths between 2000 and 2023. That number is staggering when you sit with it. Measles is one of the most contagious diseases known, with a basic reproduction number typically cited between 12 and 18.

Here's another one. The Earth's atmosphere is roughly 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, with argon and carbon dioxide making up most of the remainder. Simple chemistry, but you'd be shocked how many adults can't tell you that.

Let me hit you with some history. The Roman Empire fell in 476 AD when the last Western Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed. Though I'd argue the whole concept of a single fall date is kind of reductive, personally.

Okay, climate. Global average surface temperature has risen by approximately 1.1 degrees Celsius since the pre-industrial period, according to the IPCC. And carbon dioxide concentrations in the atmosphere have exceeded 420 parts per million in recent years, which is higher than at any point in at least the last 800,000 years based on ice core records.

One more. Lightning never strikes the same place twice. That's a classic. The Empire State Building gets hit something like twenty to twenty-five times a year, so obviously that saying doesn't hold up.

And finally, let's talk nutrition, which is where the internet loses its mind. You need to drink eight glasses of water a day, that's the rule everyone repeats. But the actual evidence for that specific number is much weaker than people assume, and total fluid intake includes water from food and other beverages.

Look, I think the lesson here is that we should all be a lot more humble about what we think we know. This stuff genuinely changed how I approach information. If you found this useful, hit subscribe, it really helps the channel out more than you'd think.

Anyway, that's the video. Thanks for watching, and I'll see you in the next one.
